name: Jet sweep
seenIn: Covered in Football 101, Lesson 22: Pre-snap motion: what a moving receiver tells you
what: The jet sweep is a run to the outside by a wide receiver. Before the snap, the receiver sprints sideways across the formation (jet motion); the ball is snapped just as he passes in front of the quarterback, who hands it to him at full speed.

Because the receiver is already running flat out when he gets the ball, he reaches the edge before linebackers can get there. The line and the tight end block toward the sideline he's heading for, so it's a race to the corner.

Teams call it to punish defenses that are slow to the outside, and to make linebackers flinch. Once a defense respects the sweep, the same motion becomes a fake: the QB keeps the ball for a run inside or a play-action pass while defenders chase the receiver.

caption: Solid white: the receiver's jet motion across the formation, the handoff in front of the QB, and his sprint around the far edge. Dashed white: the running back's fake inside. Yellow dashes: the linebackers chasing sideways.
spot: A receiver is still sprinting sideways across the formation when the ball is snapped, and the QB hands it to him as he passes, often a quick shovel-like handoff or a forward pitch. If the receiver goes by without the ball, it was a fake: watch the linebackers drift that way.
beats: Slow or overaggressive linebackers and defenses in man coverage whose cornerback has to chase the motion. Log it as a Run in the drill, even though a receiver carries it (a forward flip in front of the QB still counts as a run).
